uncited: This approach builds on [Naive Isosurface Extraction](4328-naive-isosurface-extraction.md) by operating on the tetrahedral subgrid structure.
Evaluate the scalar function at all four sample points (vertices) of the tetrahedron to obtain `surf_vals`.
Iterate through every point `v1` in `less_than_iso` and every point `v2` in `more_than_iso` to form candidate edges.
For each pair `(v1, v2)`, calculate the intersection vertex `new_vertex` using linear interpolation.
- The algorithm performs a pairwise comparison of all 'less' and 'more' points.
For a tetrahedron with 4 vertices, if 2 are less and 2 are more, this results in $2 \times 2 = 4$ intersection calculations, whereas standard MT only generates 2 edges.
- **Time Complexity:** $O(1)$ per tetrahedron, but with a higher constant factor than standard MT.
In the worst case (2 less, 2 more vertices), it performs 4 intersection calculations instead of 2.
- **Memory Complexity:** $O(1)$ auxiliary space per tetrahedron for storing partitioned lists.
- **When to use:** When simplicity of implementation is prioritized over performance and connectivity, or for educational purposes.
- **When not to use:** When high performance, mesh connectivity, or topological correctness is required.
It represents a brute-force variant of the Marching Tetrahedra algorithm, abandoning the standard case-based approach in favor of pairwise edge intersection.
